Future Community Builder

If You Owned A Community In 2076, Who Would It Be For?

Over three lessons your team will choose who lives in your community, decide what kind of place it is, and draw the blueprint you will build with LEGO. AI will help you think. You make every decision.

Lesson 1 Of 3 · 45 Minutes

Who Lives Here?

We Are Learning
  • to describe what different residents need from a community
  • to use an AI role-play prompt and judge its answers
I Can
  • build profiles for at least two residents with three needs each
  • name one thing the AI got wrong or missed
Key WordsResident: a person who lives in a placeNeed: something a person must have to live wellStereotype: an unfair idea that everyone in a group is the same
1

Mindful Minute

3 min

Breathe in for four, out for six. Now picture someone you know who is over 60. What does their neighbourhood get wrong for them?

2

Choose Your Residents

7 min

Pick two to four groups. A community for everyone is harder to design, and more interesting.

3

Build Their Profiles

15 min

Turn each group into one real person. Start from a ready-made persona or make your own, then change anything you like. Every resident needs a name, exactly three needs, and a typical day.

4

Interview A Resident With AI

12 min

This prompt is built from your profile. Copy it into a free AI tool, then ask five questions of your own. Notice the four parts: every good prompt has them.

5

Check The AI

5 min

The AI has never lived in your community. Tick what you noticed in its answers.

6

Exit Ticket

3 min
Lesson 2 Of 3 · 45 Minutes

What Kind Of Place?

We Are Learning
  • to make trade-offs with a limited budget
  • to use AI as a critic, not as the designer
I Can
  • explain why we chose some features and left others out
  • accept one AI suggestion and reject one, with a reason
Key WordsFeature: one useful thing in the communityTrade-Off: giving up one thing to get anotherSustainable: good for people and the planet for a long time
1

Mindful Minute

3 min

One slow breath with your eyes closed. It is 2076 and you open your front door. What is the first thing you want to see?

2

Set The Balance

7 min

Move each slider until your whole team agrees. There is no correct answer, only a choice you can defend.

Theatres And MuseumsNature And Animals
High-TechLow-Tech
Tall And CompactLow And Spread Out
Your Community Type

3

Spend Your 20 Points

15 min

You cannot afford everything. Watch how your residents react each time you add or remove a feature.

These are example residents. Finish Lesson 1 to see your own.

Points Left
of 20
Green Score

Residents React

You added an AI service, so your community now collects data. On paper, note what it collects and who decides how it is used.

4

Ask The Critic

12 min

This prompt contains your whole plan. The AI may criticise it. It may not redesign it.

5

The Human Decision

5 min

AI proposes. Humans decide. Go back and change your features if the critic convinced you.

6

Exit Ticket

3 min
Lesson 3 Of 3 · 45 Minutes

Put It On Paper

We Are Learning
  • to turn our decisions into a labelled blueprint
  • to record what the AI did and what we did
I Can
  • draw a blueprint with zones, features, paths and a key
  • describe my own thinking in the AI Did, I Did log
Key WordsBlueprint: a plan drawn from aboveZone: an area with one main useKey: a box that explains the colours and symbols
1

Mindful Minute

3 min

One slow breath. Think of a map you have used. What made it easy or hard to read?

2

Read Your Blueprint Brief

5 min

Everything your team decided is here. You will need one sheet of A3 paper, a pencil, a ruler and six colours.

Some of this brief is an example. Finish Lessons 1 and 2 to see your own plan.

3

Draw It In Six Steps

25 min

Select a step to see what your page should look like at that point. The example sheet is drawn from your own plan.

    Tick Each Feature When It Is On Your Paper
    Brick Colour Key For LEGO Build Day

    Use the same colours on your paper key, so your blueprint and your model match.

    4

    Question Round With AI

    7 min

    Add a short description of your drawing where the prompt asks for it. The AI will ask questions. Your team answers them out loud, then fixes the blueprint.

    5

    AI Did, I Did

    5 min

    Be honest. This log is your evidence that the thinking was yours.

    Copy your plan to paste into Padlet or your notes.
